routes.label: Track the difference between the hand positions

question: The times between \(7\) and \(8\) o’clock, correct to the nearest minute, when the hands of a clock will form an angle of \(84\) degrees are:
solution:
Both hands move, so we track their angular positions from 12. The minute hand moves \(360/60=6^\circ\) per minute, while the hour hand moves \(30/60=\frac12^\circ\) per minute.

Let \(t\) be the number of minutes after 7, with \(0<t<60\). The minute hand is at \(6t\) degrees, and the hour hand is at \(210+t/2\) degrees. Their signed difference is therefore
\[
6t-\left(210+\frac t2\right)=\frac{11t}{2}-210.
\]
During this hour, that difference increases from \(-210^\circ\) toward \(120^\circ\). An \(84^\circ\) smaller angle occurs when the difference is \(-84^\circ\) or \(84^\circ\). Differences of \(\pm276^\circ\), which would give the same smaller angle, are outside this range, as are any further full-turn possibilities.

Solving the two equations gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{11t}{2}-210=-84
&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad t=\frac{252}{11}\approx22.91,\\
\frac{11t}{2}-210=84
&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad t=\frac{588}{11}\approx53.45.
\end{aligned}
\]
Both values lie between 0 and 60. The signed difference increases steadily, so each equation gives exactly one time and these are all the possibilities. Rounding to the nearest minute gives \(\boxed{7{:}23\text{ and }7{:}53}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
